sentences.text:
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner,
learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the Informant.
2. The Petitioner is seeking pre-arrest bail in connection with G.R. Case No.1588 of 2021 pending in the Court of learned S.D.J.M., Talcher, arising out of Talcher P.S. Case NO.356 of 2021 for commission of offence punishable under Sections 419/420/120-B/ 468/ 471 of IPC.
3.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that because of his criminal proclivity,
false allegations have been made.
Hence, the Petitioner may be protected by pre-arrest bail.

4. Learned counsel for the State opposes such submission and states that there is prima facie materials so far as Petitioner is concerned for which charge sheet in the case at hand has been filed citing him as an accused.
5. Learned counsel for the Informant refers to an affidavit by which the matter is stated to have been settled inter se between the parties.

6. Considering the submission at the Bar and taking into account that that charge sheet has already been filed, this Court directs that on surrendering within three weeks hence and moving for bail, the Petitioner shall be released on bail by the learned Court in seisin on such terms as deemed just and proper.
